Gap: registered .70 - .6862 = .0138 (descriptive 6-way .6929). Single-model control .6706; every re-processing of BSCCM's own
measurements since N066 is flat or worse (attempts.md).

1. K043 (N066): the b10 direction already scores .7036; the b01 deficit sits in draw-1 evaluation labels (replicate slide .88 vs .58,

   coherence is not the bottleneck; per-marker accuracy is.
3. N076: training only on the multi-marker slides changes nothing (MM3 -.0012) -> the multi-marker cells are already fitted.
4. K033 learning curve (v5): each doubling of labelled cells +~.015-.02 GOAL (weak4 +.05) -> the model is DATA-limited on the weak

   ConvNeXt-S: stronger representation; the SSL loss was still falling at epoch 40).

Bottleneck hypothesis: LF->marker decoding on BSCCM is limited by the INFORMATION in its labelled set (few positive cells per weak marker
per draw, one marker per cell) plus evaluation-label noise (unreachable); the model already extracts what these labels support and
decodes a jointly consistent profile. Progress needs NEW information: (a) more/other labelled cells with ALL markers per cell
(S-BIAD452: 9 markers on every cell, ImageStream BF/SSC; user now allows external data), (b) a richer per-cell training signal (N074),
(c) a stronger pretrained representation (N078, external label-free pretraining).

reading only holds within-modality; if N074/N078 are flat, representation/supervision richness on the same data is also exhausted.

# N077 data scout: public label-free leukocyte data that could help BSCCM LF->marker decoding

Date 2026-11-23. Read-only scout. Searched with WebSearch and WebFetch. Nothing was downloaded.
Quotes are verbatim from the page or tool extract. Anything not checked first-hand is marked [unverified].

## Bottom line
- Only one public set gives label-free images with **many markers per cell** on human whole-blood leukocytes: **S-BIAD452** (Lippeveld/Saeys, ImageStream). It is the top pick for joint decoding.
- No other LED-array/FPM leukocyte set with markers exists apart from BSCCM's own **BSCCM-coherent**.
- No large public label-free WBC set (>BSCCM) turned up for SSL. The large label-free blood sets are RT-DC flow brightfield, which is low-res and shows deformed cells (big gap).
- Reference ceiling: DeepIFC (60x IFC, 527k PBMC) still gets only CD19 r=.61 and CD56 r=.53, against CD45 .90. So weak markers stay weak even at 3x magnification. Our CD19 .32 has headroom, but ~.6 is a realistic external ceiling.

## Ranked list (usefulness for multi-marker LF->marker)

### 1. S-BIAD452 — human WBC imaging flow cytometry (Lippeveld, Saeys, Filby et al.)  [HIGH]
- URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/BioImages/studies/S-BIAD452 ; files: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/fire/S-BIAD/452/S-BIAD452/Files/human_wbc_ifc/
- Study text: "Four human whole blood samples were assayed on an ImageStream-X MK II imaging flow cytometer." "Two samples were stained for the identification of 8 white blood cell types."
- Single 9-colour tube, so **all markers are on every cell**: "CD15 FITC, Siglec-8 PE, CD14 PE-CF594, CD19 PerCP-Cy5.5, CD3 BV421, CD45 V500, CD4 BV605, CD56 APC, CD8 APC-Cy7" (API record). Channel names in filelist.json: BF1, BF2, SSC, CD15, Siglec8, CD14, CD19, CD3, CD45, CD4, CD56, CD8. There are also unstained/eosinophil-panel samples.
- Overlap with ours: CD45, CD3, CD19, CD56, CD14 (5/8). Missing: CD16, CD123, HLA-DR.
- Size: filelist.json lists 45 entries totalling 42,233,708,651 B (~42 GB): .cif 19.2 GB, zarr single-cell stores 17.1 GB, SCIP features.parquet 4.1 GB, plus .daf files with manual gating.
- Cells: the paper's labelled WBC set holds ~98k cells: "CD4+ T-cells 17,358; CD8+ 8,022; neutrophils 59,034; monocytes 2,655; B-cells 4,256; CD56+ NKT 2,214; other NKT 1,318; eosinophils 3,156" (bioRxiv 10.1101/680975 extract). B and NK cells are few.
- Modality: "using the 60x magnification", "0.25 μm per pixel". Two BF bands (420–480 nm, 570–595 nm) and SSC darkfield (laser side scatter).
- Licence: not stated on the record. BIA policy says "all new data directly submitted to the BioImage Archive will be made available under a CC0 or CC-BY-4.0 licence" (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/bioimage-archive/help-policies). Either works for academic use.
- How to use:
  - (a) Multi-task training with a second input stem: an IFC stem feeds a shared trunk and shared heads for the 5 overlapping markers. IFC cells carry joint labels, so they teach co-expression and exclusivity (CD3/CD19/CD56).
  - (b) A source of joint marker vectors for a structured or joint decoder prior.
  - (c) Extra SSL data.
- Modality gap: medium-high. Magnification is 3x ours. TDI-flow brightfield lacks the angular LED diversity. Laser SSC is not LED darkfield. The panel is per-sample compensated fluorescence intensity, not BSCCM's fluorescence.
- Cheapest test: pull one sample's zarr (a few GB) and resample BF1+SSC to the BSCCM pixel size. Then (i) run a frozen BSCCM encoder plus a ridge probe on CD19/CD56/CD3. (ii) Reverse direction: train the IFC multi-task model, then linear-probe its trunk on BSCCM CD19/HLA-DR against the in-domain SSL encoder. Under 1 GPU-h.

### 2. BSCCM-coherent (in-domain, same instrument)  [HIGH-MEDIUM, small]
- URL: https://waller-lab.github.io/BSCCM ; Dryad https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.sxksn038s ; paper https://arxiv.org/html/2402.06191v1
- Paper: "contains 566 different illumination patterns, each corresponding to illumination by a different single LED". "BSCCM-coherent contains only all-antibodies and no antibody conditions". "each dataset also contains fluorescence images in 6 channels".
- Size: 30 GB, 4,304 cells, 128x128 12-bit (tiny version: 100 cells, 0.6 GB). Licence: the arXiv page is CC BY 4.0; the dataset licence is not stated on the project page [unverified, Dryad default CC0].
- Use: there is no modality gap. Under incoherent illumination, any pattern is the sum of single-LED images. That allows:
  - learned-illumination search (Cooke/Horstmeyer, https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04306: "optimized patterns result in up to a 45% performance improvement");
  - testing whether high-angle LEDs beyond our 24 channels carry CD19/HLA-DR signal;
  - FPM/QPI phase reconstruction as an extra input channel.
- Limits: only 4.3k cells and 'all' (pooled) labels only. Good for an evaluation or design study, too small to train a backbone.
- Cheapest test: synthesize our 24 channels from the single-LED stack, then compare a ridge/small-CNN pooled-channel r on 24 channels against all 566 LEDs (or PCA-64).

### 3. DeepIFC (Timonen et al., Cytometry A 2023)  [MEDIUM as reference/teacher, data NOT public]
- https://github.com/timonenv/DeepIFC ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.08.10.503433v2.full
- "The DeepIFC workflow and models trained on PBMC data are available under a permissible license." (repo: Apache-2.0). No data deposit found.
- Data: PBMC "n=527,107 cells", "Images were acquired at 60× magnification", BF Ch01/Ch09 + darkfield Ch12. Panel: CD45, CD14, CD19, CD8, CD3, CD56, 7-AAD.
- Per-marker r: CD45 .90, CD14 .88, CD3 .87, CD19 .61, CD56 .53, CD8 .41.

class SSLCells(RawSet):
    """Raw int16 records only (normalisation + views run batched on the GPU). Index = (row-offset, epoch) from EpochBatches."""
    def __getitem__(self, index):
        i, _epoch = index

class EpochBatches:
    """Deterministic shuffle, skip already-committed batches without reading them."""
    def __init__(self, n, bs, seed):
        self.n, self.bs, self.seed = n, bs, seed
        self.epoch, self.start = 0, 0

    @property
    def total(self):
        return self.n // self.bs

    def __len__(self):
        return self.total - self.start

    def __iter__(self):
        order = torch.randperm(self.n, generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(self.seed + self.epoch)).tolist()
        for b in range(self.start, self.total):
            yield [(i, self.epoch) for i in order[b * self.bs:(b + 1) * self.bs]]


def atomic_save(obj, path):
    path = Path(path)
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + '.tmp')
    with tmp.open('wb') as f:
        torch.save(obj, f)
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp, path)

@torch.no_grad()
def health_metrics(model, loader, gnorm):
    model.eval()
    features = []
    for raw, ph, g in loader:
        x = gnorm(raw.cuda(non_blocking=True), ph.cuda(non_blocking=True), g.cuda(non_blocking=True), 'all', True)
        x = torch.cat((x, torch.ones_like(x)), 1)                      # full view: all 24 channels present
        with torch.autocast('cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16):
            h = model(x.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last))
        features.append(h.float())
    h = torch.cat(features)
    h = h - h.mean(0)
    # Entropy of singular values, as requested (not their squares).
    sv = torch.linalg.svdvals(h)
    total = sv.sum()
    p = sv / total.clamp_min(1e-12)
    rank = torch.exp(-(p * p.clamp_min(1e-12).log()).sum())
    rank = torch.where(total > 1e-12, rank, rank.new_zeros(()))
    unit = h / h.square().sum(0).sqrt().clamp_min(1e-12)
    corr = unit.T @ unit
    d = corr.shape[0]
    if d < 2:
        raise ValueError('encoder health requires at least two features')
    offdiag = (corr.abs().sum() - corr.diag().abs().sum()) / (d * (d - 1))
    model.train()
    return {'effective_rank': rank.item(), 'mean_abs_offdiag_corr': offdiag.item()}

    p.add_argument('--proj-dim', type=int, default=256)
    p.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=15)
    p.add_argument('--rows', choices=['all', 'train'], default='all')
    p.add_argument('--exclude-batch', type=int, nargs='+', default=[])

def main():
    a = parse_args()
    stop = False

    def on_term(signum, frame):
        nonlocal stop
        stop = True

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, on_term)
    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported():
        raise RuntimeError('training requires a CUDA device with bf16 support')
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ckpt_path = out / 'ckpt.pt'
    resume_path = ckpt_path if a.resume == 'auto' else (None if a.resume == 'none' else Path(a.resume))
    if a.resume == 'none' and (ckpt_path.exists() or (out / 'encoder_final.pt').exists()):
        raise FileExistsError('refusing to overwrite an existing run with --resume none')
    if a.resume not in ('auto', 'none') and not resume_path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(resume_path)
    if a.resume == 'auto' and not ckpt_path.exists() and (out / 'encoder_final.pt').exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError('final encoder exists without ckpt.pt; use a fresh output directory')
    random.seed(a.seed)
    np.random.seed(a.seed)
    torch.manual_seed(a.seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(a.seed)
    with np.load(W + '/targets_v3.npz') as t:
        unknown = set(a.exclude_batch) - set(np.unique(t['batch']).tolist())
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f'unknown excluded batches: {sorted(unknown)}')
        keep = np.ones(len(t['split']), dtype=bool) if a.rows == 'all' else t['split'] == 0
        keep &= ~np.isin(t['batch'], a.exclude_batch)
    rows = np.flatnonzero(keep)
    if len(rows) < max(1024, a.bs):
        raise ValueError('need >=1024 eligible cells for fixed health batch and >=bs for training')
    sampler = EpochBatches(len(rows), a.bs, a.seed)
    train = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(SSLCells(rows),
                                       batch_sampler=sampler, **loader_options(a.workers, a.seed))
    health_rows = np.random.default_rng(a.seed).choice(rows, 1024, replace=False)
    health = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(RawSet(health_rows), batch_size=min(a.bs, 64),
                                        **loader_options(a.workers, a.seed + 1))
    gnorm = GPUNorm('cuda')
    model = timm.create_model(a.arch, pretrained=False, in_chans=48, num_classes=0)
    projector = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(model.num_features, 2048), nn.BatchNorm1d(2048), nn.GELU(),
                              nn.Linear(2048, 2048), nn.BatchNorm1d(2048), nn.GELU(),
                              nn.Linear(2048, a.proj_dim))
    model = model.cuda().to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)
    projector = projector.cuda()
    params = list(model.parameters()) + list(projector.parameters())
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=a.lr, weight_decay=0.05)
    total_steps, warm_steps = a.epochs * sampler.total, 2 * sampler.total

    def lr_factor(step):
        if step < warm_steps:
            return (step + 1) / warm_steps
        progress = min(1.0, (step - warm_steps) / max(1, total_steps - warm_steps))
        return 0.5 * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * progress))

    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(opt, lr_factor)
    epoch = batch = step = 0
    # sums of loss/pred/reg times batch size, image count, elapsed epoch seconds.
    accum = np.zeros(5, dtype=np.float64)
    resume_rng = None
    config = {k: v for k, v in vars(a).items() if k not in ('out', 'resume', 'max_steps', 'workers')}
    if resume_path is not None and resume_path.exists():
        s = torch.load(resume_path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=False)
        if s['config'] != config or not np.array_equal(s['rows'], rows):
            raise ValueError('resume configuration or eligible rows differ from checkpoint')
        model.load_state_dict(s['model'])
        projector.load_state_dict(s['projector'])
        opt.load_state_dict(s['opt'])
        sched.load_state_dict(s['sched'])
        epoch, batch, step = s['epoch'], s['batch'], s['step']
        accum = np.asarray(s['accum'], dtype=np.float64)
        resume_rng = s['rng']
        print(f'resumed epoch={epoch} next_batch={batch} step={step}', flush=True)
        del s
    import wandb
    run = wandb.init(project=os.environ.get('WANDB_PROJECT', 'BSCCM'),
                     name=out.resolve().name, id=out.resolve().name, mode='offline',
                     resume='allow', dir=str(out),
                     config={**vars(a), 'slurm_job_id': os.environ.get('SLURM_JOB_ID'),
                             'n_rows': len(rows), 'transductive': a.rows == 'all'})
    if resume_rng is not None:
        restore_rng(resume_rng)
        del resume_rng
    last_save = time.monotonic()

    def save():
        nonlocal last_save
        atomic_save(dict(model=model.state_dict(), projector=projector.state_dict(),
                         opt=opt.state_dict(), sched=sched.state_dict(), epoch=epoch,
                         batch=batch, step=step, rng=rng_state(), accum=accum,
                         config=config, rows=rows), ckpt_path)
        last_save = time.monotonic()

    model.train()
    projector.train()
    while epoch < a.epochs:
        if stop or (a.max_steps and step >= a.max_steps):
            save()
            run.finish()
            return
        sampler.epoch, sampler.start = epoch, batch
        tick = time.monotonic()
        for raw, ph, g in train:
            x = gnorm(raw.cuda(non_blocking=True), ph.cuda(non_blocking=True), g.cuda(non_blocking=True), 'all', True)
            gen = torch.Generator(device='cuda').manual_seed(a.seed * 1_000_003 + step)   # deterministic per step (resume-safe)
            views = make_views_batch(x, a.arm, a.views, gen)
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            zs = []
            # Separate forwards preserve per-view BN statistics, with one joint loss.
            for x in views:
                x = x.cuda(non_blocking=True).contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)
                with torch.autocast('cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16):
                    zs.append(projector(model(x)))
            loss, pred, reg = ssl_loss(zs, a.lam)
            if not torch.isfinite(loss):
                raise FloatingPointError(f'nonfinite loss at step {step}')
            loss.backward()
            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, 3.0, error_if_nonfinite=True)
            opt.step()
            sched.step()
            vals = torch.stack((loss.detach(), pred.detach(), reg.detach())).cpu().numpy()
            now = time.monotonic()
            accum[:3] += vals * a.bs
            accum[3] += a.bs
            accum[4] += now - tick
            step += 1
            batch += 1
            if stop or (a.max_steps and step >= a.max_steps):
                save()
                run.finish()
                return
            if now - last_save >= 20 * 60:
                save()
            tick = time.monotonic()
        metrics = health_metrics(model, health, gnorm)
        if accum[3] == 0:
            raise RuntimeError('epoch has no accumulated training samples')
        record = dict(epoch=epoch + 1, loss=float(accum[0] / accum[3]),
                      pred=float(accum[1] / accum[3]), sigreg=float(accum[2] / accum[3]),
                      secs=float(accum[4]), imgs_per_s=float(accum[3] / max(accum[4], 1e-12)),
                      **metrics)
        print(json.dumps(record, allow_nan=False), flush=True)
        run.log(record, step=step)
        epoch += 1
        batch = 0
        accum = np.zeros(5, dtype=np.float64)
        save()
        if stop:
            run.finish()
            return
    # Export encoder only, CPU tensors; retain just the latest full checkpoint.
    atomic_save({k: v.detach().cpu() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}, out / 'encoder_final.pt')
    run.finish()

class EpochBatches:

    def __init__(self, n, bs, seed):

Cheapest falsifier: coarse 32² decoder versus scalar-only IFC training at matched encoder steps, then b01 transfer/control, **~3 GPU-h**; stop if improved pixels do not improve markers. Build **2–3 days**; reuse N074 alignment logic, not its dataset layout.
**3. Marker-adapted transformer — NEW REPRESENTATION; challenges N053's encoder ranking.** Pretrain DINOv3-S on IFC nine-marker regression using a modality-specific patch embedding; then fine-tune every block on source BSCCM after stem warmup, encoder LR comparable to head LR. N053 already trained all blocks at LR×.1: unfreezing alone is not new. Changes are external marker supervision and physical input adaptation rather than repeated RGB weights. Expected **+0–.008**; failed N053 ViTs and ConvNeXt residual correlations .94–.96 lower confidence. Cheapest falsifier: short external adaptation, matched BSCCM high-LR/×.1 controls, **~4 GPU-h**; stop if neither beats SSL-r50. Build **1–2 days**. N078 separately tests longer in-domain SSL.
**4. Image-conditioned joint uncertainty — NEW JOINT SUPERVISION.** Fit nine means plus rank-2 covariance with marginal MSE and joint Gaussian likelihood on real IFC vectors. No observed marker enters inference; no marker combination is forbidden. Transfer shared features while retaining BSCCM masked scalar heads. Unlike exhausted BSCCM heads, these cells provide measured cross-products. Expected GOAL **+0–.003**; joint likelihood/coverage is the main opportunity because pooled consistency already differs by only .005. Cheapest falsifier: fixed IFC features, diagonal versus rank-2 covariance under donor holdout, **~.3 GPU-h**; stop without held-donor likelihood/coverage gains. Full transfer screen **~2 GPU-h**. Build **1 day**. Report vector RMSE too: better covariance need not improve means.

Distil a 566-angle teacher — NEW MEASUREMENTS; challenges “not image-limited.”** On BSCCM-coherent, synthesize deployed channels with exposure/background correction; teach a paired 24-channel student from all-angle features and pooled labels. Cheapest falsifier: source-FOV-held-out ridge, all-angle PCA versus synthesized channels, **0 GPU-h**; stop without pooled improvement. Student screen **~1 GPU-h**. Build **2 days**. Teacher improvement must survive distillation.
**6. Hybrid morphology bridge — challenges reliance on deep features alone.** Extract BF cell size/shape/texture and SSC granularity on IFC; compute corresponding BF/DF descriptors on source BSCCM with separate scaling/readouts. Concatenate descriptors with CNN features for measured marker regression, without gates/classes.
